items.evidence: After the title and a one-line run stamp ("Research run r12, 2026-10-26. Every figure below is conditional on the library of 553 volumes I searched..."), the overview's first section is "## The bottom line" with "**1. What FRUS answers directly.**", "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**" and "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**" in that order; "## Findings" begins only after Scope and "Decisions this needs from you".

Every figure names its set: "about 2,700 documents in 41 volumes whose editors headed chapters on revolutions and recognition (1895 to 1950), plus about 450 later documents from 20 Western Hemisphere volumes"; "more than nine in ten of the chapter documents cite a file number"; "about ninety chapter documents have no source citation in the index"; "mentioned in about thirty documents in eighteen volumes, 1931 to 1977"; "nearly 94,000 documents in 552 of the 553 volumes"; "The library has 57 volumes for 1861 to 1894 ... about 450 documents in 55 of them; I read only two"; "about one chapter document in fifteen"; "about three of every eight chapter documents against about one in ten of the other documents in the same volumes"; "55 of the 56 documents in the collection". A grep finds no % sign; the only "percentage" is inside the quoted 1911 Nicaragua document ("a certain percentage of the customs receipts"), a document's own words, not a figure of the report.

Every citation, in the bottom line, the findings and the block-quote attributions, is the printed edition with a link, e.g. "Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1900, Document 530, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1900/d530", "Foreign Relations of the United States: Diplomatic Papers, 1934, The American Republics, Volume V, Document 199, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1934v05/d199", "Foreign Relations of the United States, 1961–1963, Volume XII, American Republics, Document 423, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1961-63v12/d423". No shortened or unlinked form appears; a grep finds no frus id outside a history.state.gov URL. All documents cited are in the collection, which holds 56 entries (the overview cites 49 of them; the rest, such as Olney on Ecuador 1895 and Hay on Venezuela 1899, carry notes).

Part 3 states each absence as a search with its terms, volumes and controls: "I searched the whole library for the phrase, with the phrase “Department of State” as a positive control (nearly 94,000 documents in 552 of the 553 volumes) and a meaningless string as a negative control (none)" for the Estrada Doctrine ("about thirty documents in eighteen volumes, 1931 to 1977 ... the count says the doctrine is discussed, not that its text is printed"); for after 1980, "The library holds only fourteen volumes dated 1981 or later and one of them is on Latin America ... a search for the full names of Haiti's 1991 military leader and of its ousted president (Raoul Cédras; Jean-Bertrand Aristide) returned nothing, which tells us about the library and not about the world"; for before 1895, "a loose search (recognition, together with revolution, provisional government or de facto, together with a Latin American country) finds about 450 documents in 55 of them; I read only two. This is a thread not followed, not an absence." The 1947 internal study's absence rests on the editors' own note, cited to 1948 Volume IX Document 7.

Greps of the overview find no SQL keyword used as such (the only "where" hits are prose: "where the printed papers were found"), no table or column name, no file path (no /Users/, .md, .db, .py, .csv, .json, .log) and no frus volume/document string outside a history.state.gov URL (a search for "frus" digits not preceded by "/" matched nothing). Data sources are named in words only: "the offline data I have", "the bundled citation index", "the companion memo", "the search tool matches word stems".

judge:r12.rankingReason: r12: all five items pass cleanly; 56 documents 1877–1973 with every citation full and linked, every zero a controlled search, jargon glossed, and a companion collection with prose heads, a note on each document and an excerpt for each quotation. r2: exemplary measurement (every rate with its base, candidate precision admitted at 23 of 40), full linked citations, the richest resolved archival shelves; dense but exact. r10: 52 documents 1866–1980, the best quotations (Seward 1868, Nixon 1969, the 1976 restatement) and period rates with bases; its abbreviated repeat citations drop the series name but keep year, volume, document and link. r5: 56 documents, full citations throughout, plainest prose and glossed terms, honest unsearched stretches; controls stated only in the method section and the archival pointers less resolved. r1: very thorough (96 documents read, six decisions, the memoranda-before-1920 measurement), but one citation reads "(FRUS 1948, The Western Hemisphere, Volume IX, Document 7)" with no link, and it is long. r7: the deepest counts and widest span 1865–1980, but repeat citations are shortened to "(Document 109, link)" after a different volume's citation, one of them misleading in print, and part 3 lacks a negative control. r6: 43 documents and strong shelf detail (POL 16, Legal Adviser lots), but block-quote attributions such as "(1877, Document 222)" carry no series name or link. r9: tight and accurate, 34 documents with extents and access status, but repeat citations omit the series name. r11: compliant and controlled but rests on only 26 documents. r4: crisp and accurate but only 19 documents and the short form "Foreign Relations, 1913". r8: the bottom line's citations carry no links at all, the 1948 Policy Planning paper was admittedly not read, and its "cannot get" section is mostly limits of the reading. r3: cites by date and title without document numbers ("1900, Acting Secretary Hill to Minister Hart, September 8, 1900"), 38 documents, an off-topic Afghanistan document, and the odd claim that FRUS cannot give "a single list of conditions".

items.evidence: memo [N01]: "Coverage query (first tool call of the run): `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT volume_id), COUNT(*), SUM(is_front_matter), SUM(is_editorial_note) FROM document_cache;` returned **553 | 321,749 | 1,103 | 8,481**"; queries.log line 1 is that command with "-> 553|321749|1103|8481". Re-run against the database: 553|321749|1103|8481.

memo header: "Every count is conditional on the library of 553 volumes"; overview opening line: "Every figure below is conditional on the library of 553 volumes I searched"; overview Scope: "This is the full library of 553 volumes".

memo cites every document as a pair, e.g. "[Q01] frus1900/d530", "frus1948v09/d115 (“Policy Planning Staff Files: Lot No. 64–D–563”)", and §9 lists all 56 collection documents as volume_id/document_id; the overview cites each document by full title plus its history.state.gov URL carrying the pair (…/frus1900/d530).

No rowid is reported anywhere in memo, overview or collection; all identities are (volume_id, document_id). memo [N02]: "the rowid is used only inside FTS5 joins to reach `frus_documents` and is never reported". Caveat for the adjudicator: queries.log also shows `ORDER BY c.rowid` in about twenty listing queries and one exploratory range `c.rowid BETWEEN (SELECT rowid … document_id='d126') AND (SELECT rowid … 'd140')` (line 47), so the memo's "only inside FTS5 joins" is inaccurate, but no identity or reported figure rests on a rowid.

Every shown join uses both columns, e.g. [N11a] "LEFT JOIN document_sources ds ON ds.volume_id=s.volume_id AND ds.document_id=s.document_id", [N11c] "JOIN external_citations e ON e.volume_id=s.volume_id AND e.document_id=s.document_id", [N04] "LEFT JOIN document_dates dd ON dd.volume_id=s.volume_id AND dd.document_id=s.document_id"; the only rowid join is the FTS5 one (c.rowid=d.rowid).

memo [N02]: "Front matter (`is_front_matter = 1`) and editorial notes (`is_editorial_note = 1`) are excluded from every count unless said otherwise"; every reported-count SQL carries "AND c.is_front_matter=0 AND c.is_editorial_note=0" (N03, N06, N07, N08, N09, N10, N11a–c, N12); [N03] "3 scope rows were apparatus and are excluded". Six exploratory listing queries in the log (lines 22, 27, 55, 56, 101, 117) filter only is_editorial_note, but none yields a reported number.

read.py's SELECT is "SELECT header,dateline,source_note,body_text,length(body_text) FROM document_cache"; grep of queries.log and all scripts finds no SELECT of summary_text or note_text; memo [N02]: "`summary_text` and `note_text` were never selected"; overview Scope: "I did not use the library's summaries or readers' notes".

No query touches cross_references: queries.log has only ".schema … cross_references" (line 4) and no MATCH/JOIN on it; memo [N02] "No `cross_references` were used" and §11 "no use of `cross_references`".

memo [N09]: "Counting surface: FTS5 porter stems over `body_text` … stems fold “recognition” with “recognized” only if the stem agrees, so this is a candidate list, not a count of recognition decisions"; every FTS hit list is re-checked by regex, e.g. phrase_shares.txt "not recognize … STRICT 61 of 66 | TOLERANT 66 of 66" and "international obligations | non-scope … STRICT 159 of 184 | TOLERANT 178 of 184 … six hits the stemmer matched are not that phrase"; the recogn* prefix is used deliberately with a strict/tolerant split.

memo [N11a]: "`SELECT ds.citation_era, count(*) …` gave decimal 2,626 of 2,729 (record_group 59, repository Department of State), no source row 91, unrecognized 8, published 3, lot_file 1" — citation_era is read as a classification of citation form; all periodisation uses document_dates.date_iso ([N04], [N05]).

memo §4 heading "Archival scope (channels never summed)"; [N11a] "Channel one, came-from … (document_sources …)" 2,626 of 2,729; [N11c] "Channel two, pointed-at … (external_citations …)" "70 citations in 60 documents"; overview: "The two channels below answer different questions … and I have not added them together."

Each numbered figure carries its SQL inline, e.g. [N03] "SQL: `SELECT s.tier, count(*), count(distinct s.volume_id) FROM s.scope s JOIN document_cache c …`", [N09] the full 20-volume pool query, [N12] the Estrada query, [N06] both control queries; [N05] points to decade.sql on disk (its text verified); re-running N03, N04, N07, N11a, N11c, N12 reproduced every number.

[N11a] "“More than nine in ten” = 2,626 of 2,729 = 0.962"; [N07] table "1,014 of 2,729 (0.372) | 3,928 of 38,789 (0.101)"; [N08] "178 of 2,729", "95 of 2,729; 94 strict"; [N14] "84 of 2,729 chapter documents retrieved". The two percentages ("92% of the numerator", "10% of the other documents") restate table rows directly above them holding 46 of 50 and 3,928 of 38,789.

[N13]: "`frus_documents MATCH '"raoul cedras"'`, `'"jean bertrand aristide"'`, `'"cedras raoul"'` each returned 0 documents. These zeros describe the library, not the world; the positive control is the one in [N12]" ("Positive control “department of state” over the whole library: **94,049 documents in 552 volumes**"); [N06] "Negative control, string ZZZ_IMPOSSIBLE_ZZZ … returned **0** (expected 0 — met)". Re-run: all three probes 0; control 94,049|552.

[N05] "Thin cells: the 1890s (one volume, frus1899, holds 92% of the numerator), the 1900s (40 documents) and the 1950s (3 documents; the scope ends with frus1950v02)"; §7 "Thin results: channel two (12 bundled references; 70 file numbers); the 1890s and 1900s decades; the 1950s (3 documents); the post-1950 pool (448 documents, about two dozen read); everything before 1895 (two documents read). These may reflect what I read, not the corpus."

[N06] "Controls for the scoping pass, run in the same pass over the 41 scope volumes. Positive control, phrase “Department of State” … returned 41 volumes, 41 with a hit, minimum 35 documents per volume, 8,527 documents in all … Negative control, string ZZZ_IMPOSSIBLE_ZZZ … returned **0**"; the two commands are consecutive in queries.log (lines 94–95); [N12] repeats both controls for the whole library.

memo header: "The TEI XML corpus was **not** read … every phrase figure below is an index-surface figure"; [N03] "Counting surface: document_cache rows after apparatus exclusion"; [N09] "Counting surface: FTS5 porter stems over `body_text` (footnotes included)"; [N07] literal shares "Python `re`, IGNORECASE, over header+dateline+source_note+body_text, whitespace-collapsed".

The question's term is expanded as the prefix recogn* and as "recognition OR recognize", chapter titles as "nonrecogni|non-recogni", and the split is reported: [N07] "Strict = the whole words recognize/recognized/recognizes/recognizing/recognition … tolerant = any word beginning `recogn`, or inflections with any run of space, hyphen, comma, parenthesis or full stop between the words"; phrase_shares.txt "not recognize … STRICT 61 of 66 | TOLERANT 66 of 66"; phrase_shares2.txt "international obligations | non-scope … STRICT 159 of 184 | TOLERANT 178 of 184".

[N04] "Date span of the chapter scope by the index's own date (`document_dates.date_iso` …; I did **not** use the volume's series year): earliest 1895-09-06, latest 1950-06-01, undated 0"; [N05] "Numerator = scope documents dated in the decade" with decade.sql on document_dates.date_iso; intervals [N15a–e] computed from the documents' datelines. Re-run: 2729|1895-09-06|1950-06-01|0.

[N02] "No second-edition volume (ids ending Ed2) is in the chapter scope, the later pool or the collection, so no second-edition suppression was needed"; queries.log line 90 "SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT distinct volume_id FROM s.scope) WHERE volume_id LIKE '%Ed2%'" (re-run: 0); build/verify.py asserts "Ed2" not in any collection volume. Residue for the adjudicator: the library holds frus1951-54Iran and frus1951-54IranEd2, and frus1969-76ve15p2 and its Ed2, so the whole-library decade denominator for the 1950s (43,159) includes 358 Ed2 documents and the 94,049-in-552 control counts both editions; the memo does not fold or mention these, though no reported per-1,000 figure changes.

[N11a] "Channel one, came-from, chapter documents (document_sources, one row per document) … gave decimal 2,626 of 2,729 (record_group 59, repository Department of State), no source row 91, unrecognized 8, published 3, lot_file 1"; decimal_gloss.txt glosses the classes (812.00 Mexico 356, 837.00 Cuba 305 …). Re-run reproduces 2626/91/8/3/1.

[N11c] "Channel two, pointed-at, chapter documents (external_citations …) … gave **70 citations in 60 documents**; anchors: centralFileClass 70. All are file numbers of the Central Decimal File"; [N11d] "`external-citation-index.json` has references for 33 of the 41 volumes and … 12 references to 7 collections: lot:53D250 (3), lot:60D137 (3), lot:53D26 (2) …". Re-run: 70|60; 33 of 41 scope volumes are in that index; archival_json_out.json "pointed" sums to 12 over 7.

Section heading "Archival scope (channels never summed)"; every count is tagged "Channel one, came-from" or "Channel two, pointed-at"; overview lists "*Series the printed documents came from (channel one…)*" and "*Series the footnotes cite without printing (channel two)*" and says "I have not added them together".

[N11a–d] name and use `central-files-index.json`, `series-facts-index.json`, `lot-claimants-index.json`, `external-citation-index.json`, `collection-usage-index.json`, `collection-authority.json`, `decimal-class-labels.json`; the scripts resolve_lots.py, archival_json.py, pre1906.py and decimal_gloss.py on disk open those files from /Applications/FRUS Explorer.app/Contents/Resources/, with outputs archival_json_out.json, pre1906_out.txt, decimal_gloss.txt.

[N11a] "record_group 59"; [N11b] "despatches Venezuela 1835–1906 roll 188967467 (file unit 177380736) … Colombia … roll 189300896 … Ecuador … roll 189312130" and "Lot No. 64–D–563 … NAID 1136548 … entry A1 558-D, RG 59"; [N11d] "53D26 NAID 2108774, A1 1130"; overview channel one names "Central decimal file, Record Group 59" and "lot 64 D 563".

[N11b] "The one lot-file source in the chapter scope is frus1948v09/d115 (“Policy Planning Staff Files: Lot No. 64–D–563”). `resolve_lots.py 64D563`: `central-files-index.json` lotFiles gives NAID 1136548, “Chronological Files”, entry A1 558-D, RG 59; `series-facts-index.json`: … 5 linear feet 3 inches, 1947–1962, accessStatus Unrestricted; `lot-claimants-index.json` lists **12** series claiming the lot". Verified: document_sources row for that pair is lot_file "Policy Planning Staff Files: Lot No. 64–D–563: PPS Papers"; central-files-index lotFiles 64D563 → naId 1136548, A1 558-D; series facts decode to Unrestricted, 1947–1962, 5 linear feet 3 inches; 12 claimant series. The pointed-at lots 53D26→2108774, 53D444→2168520, 56D625→2092759, 66D95→2839192 also verified.

[N07] false-friend table for the question's term: "recogn* (prefix) | 1,014 of 2,729 (0.372) | 3,928 of 38,789 (0.101)" beside the control "“department of state” | 333 of 2,729 (0.122) | 8,194 of 38,789 (0.211)", then the literal shares of those hit lists: "recogn* (prefix) | scope documents | FTS recogn* | M=1014 | evenly spaced 40 n=40 | STRICT 40 of 40 | TOLERANT 40 of 40" and the same for the control. Re-run reproduces 1,014/2,729 and 3,928/38,789.

Each change claim is bracketed by retrieved documents on both sides: "enforced it against El Salvador's General Martínez from 1931 until January 1934, and abandoned it in 1936" rests on frus1931v02/d232 (1931-12-20), frus1934v05/d257 (1934-01-26) and frus1936v05/d112 (1936-04-30), with [N15c] measuring the interval ("768 days = 2.10 years"); "In the 1950s the Department recognized quickly … Under Kennedy it tried the opposite" cites 1955/1957/1959 documents and then 1962/1963 documents; the decade table is explicitly not read as a prevalence trend ("the shape is a product of which chapters the editors wrote").

memo §8 lists all 22 quotations with pair, offset, length and SELECT, e.g. "[Q01] frus1900/d530, offset 1439, 447 characters, exact substring of body_text: yes. SELECT: `SELECT body_text FROM document_cache WHERE volume_id = 'frus1900' AND document_id = 'd530';`". I checked all 22 against the database: each is an exact substring at the stated offset, and each appears verbatim in the overview with its citation. The five other quoted strings in the overview ("Department of State", "international obligations", "Revolution in…" etc.) are declared in §7 as search phrases and editors' chapter-title formulas, not document quotations.

[N14] "Documents retrieved whole: **124** distinct (volume_id, document_id) pairs written by `read.py` … Of these, 84 lie in the chapter scope (84 of 2,729 chapter documents retrieved). The collection holds **56** documents, all retrieved whole; I displayed 55 of them in full and one in part … Documents read in the 1877–1878 sample: 2"; reading_ledger.csv has 124 rows and raw/ holds 124 files; overview: "I read in full 55 of the 56 documents in the collection and part of the other".

Every share carries its numerator and denominator where used: [N07] "1,014 of 2,729 (0.372)"; [N08] "“de facto”, about one in fifteen: 178 of 2,729", "about a hundred: 95 of 2,729; 94 strict"; [N11a] "“More than nine in ten” = 2,626 of 2,729 = 0.962"; phrase lines "STRICT 94 of 95 | TOLERANT 95 of 95". The only percentages ("92%", "10%") sit in the sentence under the table row that holds 46 of 50 and 3,928 of 38,789.

queries.log is headed "commands against resources, in order" (no claim of verbatim completeness), marks "entries below were written after the fact", and closes with an explicit "ELIDED:" paragraph naming every helper script and what is not reproduced; the memo maps numbers to files ("SQL in `decade.sql`" for N05, "Output file `phrase_shares.txt`" for N08, "`archival_json.py` (output `archival_json_out.json`)" for N11d, `decimal_gloss.txt`, `pre1906_out.txt`, `reading_ledger.csv`), and build/stats.json holds every reported figure with POOL_SQL and PRE_SQL. Gap noted: resolve_lots.py's output (the NAID/entry/access lookups of N11b/N11d) is not kept on disk, though I verified those values directly in the bundled JSON.

A scan of overview.md finds no SELECT/FROM/WHERE, no column or table name (no document_cache, body_text, volume_id, rowid, underscore tokens), no .json/.db/.md/.py/.csv name and no path; data are described in words ("the library's summaries or readers' notes", "the bundled citation index", "the companion memo"). Documents are cited by full title and public URL ("Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1900, Document 530, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1900/d530"); the volume/document id appears only as the tail of those history.state.gov URLs, never as a bare pair.

Each overview number names its set and traces through memo §10 (46 rows, line numbers verified: N01→10, N03→17, N07→42, N08→61, N11a–d→72–75, N12→79, N13→80, N14→84, N15a–e→88–92, N16→93, N17→94, Q01–Q22→112–133): "about 2,700 documents in 41 volumes whose editors headed chapters on revolutions and recognition" → N03 2,729/41; "nearly 94,000 documents in 552 of the 553 volumes" → N12; "about one chapter document in fifteen" → N08 178 of 2,729; "about three of every eight chapter documents against about one in ten" → N07 0.372/0.101; "3 October to 14 December 1963, ten weeks" → N15e; lot and roll identifiers → N11b/N11d.

The overview opens with "## The bottom line" in three numbered parts: "**1. What FRUS answers directly.**" citing the documents (frus1900/d530, frus1948v09/d7, frus1917/d379 … by title and URL); "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**" with "*Series the printed documents came from (channel one…)*" (Central decimal file RG 59; pre-1906 despatch/instruction rolls; PPS lot 64 D 563) and "*Series the footnotes cite without printing (channel two)*"; "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**" with the establishing searches: "I searched the whole library for the phrase, with the phrase “Department of State” as a positive control (nearly 94,000 documents in 552 of the 553 volumes) and a meaningless string as a negative control (none)", the fourteen post-1980 volumes and full-name probes, and the pre-1895 loose search.

score:r12.notes: All four required files are present (memo.md 285 lines, overview.md 104 lines, collection.fruscollection with 56 documents / 22 excerpts / 6 headings / 7 prose / 1 generated block, queries.log 133 lines), plus the helper scripts, scope.db, raw/ (124 documents), reading_ledger.csv, display_ledger.csv, script outputs and build/ (stats.json, verify.py). Independent verification against the read-only database: coverage 553|321749|1103|8481; scope 2,729 documents in 41 volumes (A 1,886/36, B 843/9); date span 1895-09-06 to 1950-06-01, undated 0; document_sources 2626/91/8/3/1; external_citations 70 in 60; recogn* 1,014 of 2,729 vs 3,928 of 38,789; Estrada doctrine 28 in 18 volumes 1931–1977 (none in an Ed2 volume); control 94,049 in 552; 14 volumes >= frus1981; 57 pre-1895 volumes; all three full-name probes 0; all 22 quotations exact substrings at the stated offsets and present in the overview; all N15 interval dates match document_dates. Bundled JSON: 64D563 -> NAID 1136548 (A1 558-D, Unrestricted, 1947–1962, 5 linear feet 3 inches), 12 claimant series; the four pointed-at lots resolve as stated; 33 of 41 scope volumes in external-citation-index. Residues recorded inside the items rather than scored as violations: (1) S5 — the library holds first and second editions of frus1951-54Iran and frus1969-76ve15p2, so the whole-library 1950s decade denominator (43,159) carries 358 Ed2 documents and the whole-library control counts both editions; the memo's Ed2 check covered the scope, pool and collection only (no reported per-1,000 figure changes); (2) I2 — the memo's claim that rowid is used only in FTS5 joins is inaccurate (ORDER BY c.rowid in listing queries and one rowid BETWEEN range in an exploratory listing), though no identity or figure rests on a rowid; (3) P6 — resolve_lots.py's output is not kept on disk; (4) queries.log names chap2_early.txt, which does not exist (the files are chap2_a/b/c.txt); (5) the bare-surname probes 'cedras' and 'aristide' are logged and expressly withdrawn in favour of full-name probes. The refuter/ directory (written 00:45, after the run's files) was not used for scoring. Task-text instructions were treated as the workflow step only; no file outside the named run directory, rubric, database and app Resources was read for this scoring.
